title: Psychophysiological investigations for promoting cognitive capacity and physical health with short bouts of physical activity during sedentary work
summary: Prolonged sitting is common in everyday working life and is associated with physical and mental load as well as reduced cognitive performance. Movement breaks can promote attention, recovery, and well-being, but it is unclear which type, duration, and frequency are particularly effective. This study therefore examines how short and long, moderate activity breaks compare to passive breaks during a simulated workday in terms of their impact on cognitive performance, subjective experience, and physiological functions. Reaction times, subjective states (e.g., mental load, mental fatigue), and objective parameters such as heart rate variability, muscle activity, and brain activity are recorded. The aim is to gain evidence for health-promoting break design in sedentary office work.
conditions: No health problems in the narrow sense are being investigated. The short-term effects of exercise on a (neuro)physiological level are being investigated.

interventions.name:
Simulated work tasks: 4x15 min & 4x10 min
Cognitive tasks: 4x 10 min & 4x 5 min
Break condition:
PAN (Physical Activity – None): 2 × 15 minutes of passive sitting breaks
Lunch break: 30 min
Total duration including preparation time: approx. 6 hours

Simulated work tasks: 4x15 min & 4x10 min
Cognitive tasks: 4x 10 min & 4x 5 min
Break condition:
PAL (Physical Activity – Long): 2 × 15 min active exercise breaks on a treadmill
Lunch break: 30 min
Total duration including preparation time: approx. 6 hours

Simulated work tasks: 4x15 min & 4x10 min
Cognitive tasks: 4x 10 min & 4x 5 min
Break condition:
PAS (Physical Activity – Short): 6 × 5 min active exercise breaks on a treadmill
Lunch break: 30 min
Total duration including preparation time: approx. 6 hours

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Healthy according to medical history and clinical examination
- Very good written and spoken German
- Current office work experience or sedentary work of >4 hours/day
Exclusion criteria:
- Previous neurological, cardiovascular, or musculoskeletal conditions
- Use of medications that affect cognitive or physiological parameters
- Pregnancy
